phase3_findings.description: docs/external/rule-sets.md line 66 says confirmed_against_production = true is required, but Source.confirmed_against_production (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:123) is a required StrictBool: a file with false loads, warns at startup, and its requests are refused. The same page (lines 89, 99, 129) and the internal doc contradict line 66.
The 'no such rule set' line covers only a name missing from the file; select_rule_set also gives it for a name that is not a string or non-Boolean integer (2.0, true, [2]).
The 'rule-set key missing' line omits that a _meta with more than 64 keys also gets this refusal.
RuleSetsConfig can hold a file path with _loaded None; every consumer checks loaded, so such a config would skip the guard silently. No current path builds it.
CatalogConfirmation.confirmed is writable, LoadedRuleSets is not frozen, and list fields of frozen _Record models are mutable in place.
RuleSetSelection has no construction-time validation; only select_rule_set enforces validity and set_rule_set_selection accepts any instance.
TableRule.row_rule: Any = None is a field that exists only to be rejected via model_fields_set.
Criterion 34 (show_details profile still served under the guard) is checked only for the selection through a fake agent; no test sends SQL through the guarded chain under that profile.
The fail-closed branches of _check_conversation_owner (no owner_id lookup; resolver or store raises) are untested.
test_refused_before_execution uses SELECT * with refuse_whole_row_selects on, so the whole-row guard may refuse first; the live test cannot attribute those refusals to the rule-set guard.
